noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Stakeholders’ engagement, community building and support for communication for EU Nature conservation policy
procedureTitle: Stakeholders’ engagement, community building and support for communication for EU Nature conservation policy
description: The general objective of this tender is to build a strong and engaged Natura 2000 community of stakeholders and citizens that supports EU policy implementation and enhances the visibility of the Commission’s actions on nature conservation, in particular: a) Establish and manage an online EU Nature Platform: a user-friendly platform to support authorities and stakeholders in implementing EU nature legislation, foster interaction and community building, and provide access to reference documents, best practices, success stories, news, and relevant activities at EU, national and regional level. b) Enhance Natura 2000 communication activities: increase awareness of the network and related EU policy objectives among the general public, improve recognition of the Natura 2000 logo, and establish a positive connection with EU nature protection efforts.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – European Monitoring of Biodiversity in Agricultural Landscapes (EMBAL) 2028
procedureTitle: European Monitoring of Biodiversity in Agricultural Landscapes (EMBAL) 2028
description: OBJECTIVES: The general objectives of this contract are to contribute towards i) the establishment of a robust data series on the state of biodiversity in agricultural landscapes in the EU, and ii) a better understanding of (the impacts of policy actions on) the biodiversity trends in agricultural landscapes at the EU and national level. The specific objectives of this contract are i) to undertake the EMBAL field survey in all EU Member States in 2028 and 2029, and ii) to analyse the collected data. The contract will survey at least 4500 sites in each year (i.e. undertake at least 9 000 site-surveys across the two years), strictly following the EMBAL survey protocol and technical guidelines as prepared and executed in the EMBAL survey 2022/2023. TASKS: 1) Preparation of the field survey (including sampling strategy and design, pre-processing of monitoring sites, selection and recruitment of surveyors, material and equipment, digitised data workflow, helpdesk, quality control and contingency planning); 2) Execution of the field survey; 3) Data post-processing; 4) Data analysis; 5) Organisation of a conference to present the results. KEY DOCUMENTS AND LINKS: 1) EMBAL survey protocol and technical guidelines: https://biodiversity.europa.eu/europes-biodiversity/nature-restoration/reference-portal-for-nature-restoration-regulation/documentation/embal-toolkit.7z 2) EMBAL 2022/2023 dataset: https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/723355a8-e549-4691-9c0d-83ab7fc7a0c4 3) EMBAL 2022/2023 analytical report: https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/a4444ad4-16b0-11f1-8870-01aa75ed71a1/language-en 4) EMBAL 2022/2023 appendix to the analytical report: https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/8f047e20-16af-11f1-8870-01aa75ed71a1/language-en

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – FRAMEWORK CONTRACT ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT TO THE NITRATES DIRECTIVE, AGRICULTURE, SOIL AND FOREST POLICIES
procedureTitle: FRAMEWORK CONTRACT ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT TO THE NITRATES DIRECTIVE, AGRICULTURE, SOIL AND FOREST POLICIES
description: Our unit ENV.D1 needs technical assistance and scientific advice on various policies the unit is working on. A Framework contract has been created to cover this need. Specifically, our unit has identified a need for technical and scientific advice in the following areas: a) on agricultural related EU policies and initiatives as well as on the environmental dimension of agriculture and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP.); b) on aspects related to the implementation of the Nitrates Directive and the follow-up of the evaluation of the Nitrates Directive; c) on the implementation of the Soil Monitoring Law (SML); d) on the implementation and follow-up of the EU Forest Strategy and forest related aspects of environmental policy and actions on integrated wildfire risk management. Area a) and b) will be covered by Lot 1; Area c) by Lot 2; Area d) by Lot 3

noticeTitle: Belgium – Technical analysis or consultancy services – Inter-institutional single framework contract to support the monitoring of LIFE projects, communication and other support services for the implementation of the LIFE programme
procedureTitle: Inter-institutional single framework contract to support the monitoring of LIFE projects, communication and other support services for the implementation of the LIFE programme
description: CINEA and DG ENV require substantial external support in the following areas: 1. Monitoring of LIFE projects, including action grants and operating grants: around 1 000 grants are to be monitored across a wide thematic and geographical coverage. There is a need for an external team of monitors covering the different thematic areas and possessing knowledge of the relevant national or local contexts and languages, in order to ensure proper monitoring of the projects and to provide support where issues arise. 2. Communication on the LIFE programme and project achievements, with a view to outreach and potential replication: this includes, for example, social media, Info Days, the LIFE Awards, other ad hoc events, participation in third-party events, project news, newsletters, and publications. It should be emphasised that LIFE grants support actions at local, regional, and national level that are close to citizens and generate tangible environmental, climate and health benefits. There is therefore a significant volume of material and strong potential to promote a positive image of the EU. 3. Other related activities include policy feedback events and studies or activities, whether online or in-person, upon request from the parent DGs, namely ENV, CLIMA and ENER; annual Welcome Meetings for new projects; and support to projects aimed at facilitating commercial success. Activities will take place in the EU, in third countries associated with the LIFE Programme: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/life/guidance/list3rdcountryparticipation_life_en.pdf and, very rarely, in overseas countries and territories, with fewer than 10 project visits estimated over the duration of the framework contract: https://international-partnerships.ec.europa.eu/countries/overseas-countries-and-territories_en

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Support to stakeholders for implementation & mainstreaming of Environmental Footprint (EF) methods
procedureTitle: Support to stakeholders for implementation & mainstreaming of Environmental Footprint (EF) methods
description: The objective of this contract is to ensure input from and the participation of environmental NGOS, consumer NGOs and organizations representing SMEs into relevant existing & any future expert groups and any other aspects related to the Environmental Footprint (EF) methods (see below). The Environmental Footprint (EF ) Steering Committee and the Technical Advisory Board Expert Groups. The first group includes representatives of the European Commission, Member States, main stakeholder groups (environmental NGOs, consumers and SMEs) and economic sectors. The second group includes environmental footprint and life cycle assessment experts. In these expert groups other EF related aspects such as methodological choices of the EF methods or specific modelling requirements of the datasets are discussed. For supporting the potential implementation of the Green Claims Directive, the Commission may create a new expert group. The representation of the SMEs and environmental and consumer NGOs is crucial to ensure that its implementation is balanced and inclusive.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Technical analysis or consultancy services – Inter-institutional single framework contract to support the monitoring of LIFE projects (action and operating grants), communication about the LIFE programme and other related activities
procedureTitle: Inter-institutional single framework contract to support the monitoring of LIFE projects (action and operating grants), communication about the LIFE programme and other related activities
description: CINEA and DG ENV require substantial external support in the following areas: 1. Monitoring of LIFE projects, including action grants and operating grants: around 1 000 grants are to be monitored across a wide thematic and geographical coverage. There is a need for an external team of monitors covering the different thematic areas and possessing knowledge of the relevant national or local contexts and languages, in order to ensure proper monitoring of the projects and to provide support where issues arise. 2. Communication on the LIFE programme and project achievements, with a view to outreach and potential replication: this includes, for example, social media, Info Days, the LIFE Awards, other ad hoc events, participation in third-party events, project news, newsletters, and publications. It should be emphasised that LIFE grants support actions at local, regional, and national level that are close to citizens and generate tangible environmental, climate and health benefits. There is therefore a significant volume of material and strong potential to promote a positive image of the EU. 3. Other related activities include policy feedback events and studies or activities, whether online or in-person, upon request from the parent DGs, namely ENV, CLIMA and ENER; annual Welcome Meetings for new projects; and support to projects aimed at facilitating commercial success. Activities will take place in the EU, in third countries associated with the LIFE Programme: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/life/guidance/list3rdcountryparticipation_life_en.pdf and, very rarely, in overseas countries and territories, with fewer than 10 project visits estimated over the duration of the framework contract: https://international-partnerships.ec.europa.eu/countries/overseas-countries-and-territories_en

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Level(s) Maintenance
procedureTitle: Level(s) Maintenance
description: The general objective of the contract is to keep Level(s) up to date in relation to the developing ecosystem in which the assessment framework is situated. Beyond policy development, this includes e.g. evolving standards of both technical and cost nature, as well as LCA software and databases. As Level(s) is developed with the clear objective of being firmly anchored in the current ecosystem, based on existing standards and link to support tools, the framework requires regular updates to continue to maximise its relevance and drive market as well as policy development. The specific objective of the contract is to ensure that Level(s) is firmly linked to EU policy impacting buildings, as well as to ensure that Level(s) is attractive to use and provide technical support at a relevant level.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – SUPPORT TO POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LEGISLATION FOR PREVENTION, PREPARATION AND RESPONSE OF MAJOR ACCIDENTS INVOLVING CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES
procedureTitle: SUPPORT TO POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LEGISLATION FOR PREVENTION, PREPARATION AND RESPONSE OF MAJOR ACCIDENTS INVOLVING CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES
description: The purchase aims to provide administrative, scientific and technical support to the Commission and Member States for implementation and development of EU policy associated with the prevention and control of major-accident hazard (Seveso III Directive). In particular the project will aim to provide assistance to the Commission in following areas: - to promote exchanges and sharing of information, good practices and lessons learnt on implementation of the Seveso-III Directive, with and between Member States. - to support the work of the Technical Working Groups on Inspections (TWG2) promoting common approaches to Seveso-III Directive implementation across Member States and consistent inspection and risk management across 11 000 highly diverse industrial sites covered by the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide technical assistance for the drafting of technical documentations and guidances supporting harmonised implementation of some provisions of the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide expertise, on an ad hoc basis, on some technical issues related to the implementation of the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide scientific support to the European Commission for risks and accidents analysis and for dissemination of lessons learnt. This purchase is necessary to address the implementation issues identified in the MS national reports on implementation of the Seveso III Directive and to take over tasks currently performed by the Major Accidents Hazard Bureau whose activities should be discontnued by the end of the year.
buyerDepartment: ENV.B - Competitive Circular Economy & Clean Industrial Policy

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Support to the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund
procedureTitle: Support to the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund
description: The objective of this contract is to support the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund, to ensure the continuation of the informal process on DSI until COP17, and offer opportunities to build mutual trust and common understanding amongst Parties and stakeholders involved. For this, a workshop would take place in the first semester of 2026, with a view to initiate in-depth discussion on the critical unresolved issues of Decision 16/2, to maintain the momentum on CBD COP16 Decision 16/2, and to promote contribution to the Cali Fund. A second workshop to strengthen the dialogue may be needed in the second half of 2026, with a view to continue discussion on outstanding issues and prepare the ground for negotiations at CBD COP17 in October 2026.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Supporting moth monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation
procedureTitle: Supporting moth monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation
description: The aim of the contract is to facilitate the monitoring of night active moths that will be undertaken by Member States in the framework of the Nature Restoration Regulation. For this purpose, the contract will: (1) improve the accuracy and species coverage of artificial intelligence-based image recognition as a means of identifying night active moths to the species level, and (2) develop capacity building activities in order to enhance the taxonomic expertise for moths in Member States, where it is currently lacking.

For this purpose, the contract will: (1) improve the accuracy and species coverage of artificial intelligence-based image recognition as a means of identifying night active moths to the species level, and (2) develop capacity building activities in order to enhance the taxonomic expertise for moths in Member States, where it is currently lacking.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Stakeholders’ engagement, community building and support for communication for EU Nature conservation policy
procedureTitle: Stakeholders’ engagement, community building and support for communication for EU Nature conservation policy
description: The general objective of this tender is to build a strong and engaged Natura 2000 community of stakeholders and citizens that supports EU policy implementation and enhances the visibility of the Commission’s actions on nature conservation, in particular: a) Establish and manage an online EU Nature Platform: a user-friendly platform to support authorities and stakeholders in implementing EU nature legislation, foster interaction and community building, and provide access to reference documents, best practices, success stories, news, and relevant activities at EU, national and regional level. b) Enhance Natura 2000 communication activities: increase awareness of the network and related EU policy objectives among the general public, improve recognition of the Natura 2000 logo, and establish a positive connection with EU nature protection efforts.

procedureTitle: Support to stakeholders for implementation & mainstreaming of Environmental Footprint (EF) methods
description: The objective of this contract is to ensure input from and the participation of environmental NGOS, consumer NGOs and organizations representing SMEs into relevant existing & any future expert groups and any other aspects related to the Environmental Footprint (EF) methods (see below). The Environmental Footprint (EF ) Steering Committee and the Technical Advisory Board Expert Groups. The first group includes representatives of the European Commission, Member States, main stakeholder groups (environmental NGOs, consumers and SMEs) and economic sectors. The second group includes environmental footprint and life cycle assessment experts. In these expert groups other EF related aspects such as methodological choices of the EF methods or specific modelling requirements of the datasets are discussed. For supporting the potential implementation of the Green Claims Directive, the Commission may create a new expert group. The representation of the SMEs and environmental and consumer NGOs is crucial to ensure that its implementation is balanced and inclusive.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Support for the implementation of the EU pledge on three billion additional trees by 2030
procedureTitle: Support for the implementation of the EU pledge on three billion additional trees by 2030
description: The EU pledge for three billion additional trees in the EU was announced in 2020 (EU Biodiversity Strategy). The implementation of the pledge depends greatly on initiatives at national and subnational level. A roadmap for its implementation with milestones was published in 2021 (EU Forest Strategy). Building on the accomplished milestones (https://environment.ec.europa.eu/strategy/biodiversity-strategy-2030/3-billion-trees_en), the contractor will further promote the implementation of the EU pledge. noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – SUPPORT TO POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LEGISLATION FOR PREVENTION, PREPARATION AND RESPONSE OF MAJOR ACCIDENTS INVOLVING CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES
procedureTitle: SUPPORT TO POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LEGISLATION FOR PREVENTION, PREPARATION AND RESPONSE OF MAJOR ACCIDENTS INVOLVING CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES
description: The purchase aims to provide administrative, scientific and technical support to the Commission and Member States for implementation and development of EU policy associated with the prevention and control of major-accident hazard (Seveso III Directive). In particular the project will aim to provide assistance to the Commission in following areas: - to promote exchanges and sharing of information, good practices and lessons learnt on implementation of the Seveso-III Directive, with and between Member States. - to support the work of the Technical Working Groups on Inspections (TWG2) promoting common approaches to Seveso-III Directive implementation across Member States and consistent inspection and risk management across 11 000 highly diverse industrial sites covered by the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide technical assistance for the drafting of technical documentations and guidances supporting harmonised implementation of some provisions of the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide expertise, on an ad hoc basis, on some technical issues related to the implementation of the Seveso-III Directive. - to provide scientific support to the European Commission for risks and accidents analysis and for dissemination of lessons learnt. This purchase is necessary to address the implementation issues identified in the MS national reports on implementation of the Seveso III Directive and to take over tasks currently performed by the Major Accidents Hazard Bureau whose activities should be discontnued by the end of the year.
buyerDepartment: ENV.B - Competitive Circular Economy & Clean Industrial Policy

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Support to the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund
procedureTitle: Support to the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund
description: The objective of this contract is to support the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund, to ensure the continuation of the informal process on DSI until COP17, and offer opportunities to build mutual trust and common understanding amongst Parties and stakeholders involved. For this, a workshop would take place in the first semester of 2026, with a view to initiate in-depth discussion on the critical unresolved issues of Decision 16/2, to maintain the momentum on CBD COP16 Decision 16/2, and to promote contribution to the Cali Fund. A second workshop to strengthen the dialogue may be needed in the second half of 2026, with a view to continue discussion on outstanding issues and prepare the ground for negotiations at CBD COP17 in October 2026.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Level(s) Maintenance
procedureTitle: Level(s) Maintenance
description: The general objective of the contract is to keep Level(s) up to date in relation to the developing ecosystem in which the assessment framework is situated. Beyond policy development, this includes e.g. evolving standards of both technical and cost nature, as well as LCA software and databases. As Level(s) is developed with the clear objective of being firmly anchored in the current ecosystem, based on existing standards and link to support tools, the framework requires regular updates to continue to maximise its relevance and drive market as well as policy development. The specific objective of the contract is to ensure that Level(s) is firmly linked to EU policy impacting buildings, as well as to ensure that Level(s) is attractive to use and provide technical support at a relevant level.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Preparatory Action project for EU Biodiversity Observation Coordination Centre (EBOCC)
procedureTitle: Preparatory Action project for EU Biodiversity Observation Coordination Centre (EBOCC)
description: The contract will pilot and test the biodiversity observation coordination centre and monitoring framework on the basis of the EuropaBON proposal. In this way, the contract will contribute to better availability, coherence and accessibility of biodiversity data in support of the EU biodiversity policy implementation at national, EU and global level, and support a coherent, structured and cost-effective EU approach to systematic biodiversity observation. This will streamline biodiversity data flows and reduce administrative burden in Member States with regard to biodiversity monitoring and reporting.

procedureTitle: Affordable and low environmental impact housing by more efficient use of existing building stock

The more specific objectives are about providing a clear picture regarding how different kinds of building policy can impact sufficiency measures and, moreover, how better data related to sufficiency can be generated and shared. procedureTitle: Support for modelling better integrated biodiversity-mitigation-adaptation policies and measures
description: The contract will fill some severe knowledge gaps identified in the impact of 2040 climate targets and thereby be a direct contribution to the Green Deal’s call for increasing synergies between climate and biodiversity actions. Specifically, it will 1) better integrate the impacts of climate change and of natural disturbances impacts (e.g. forest fires) on biodiversity, in models used to design climate, energy and land policies and 2) ensure that the scenarios used in biodiversity impact assessment (e.g. BIOCLIMA) are better aligned with the scenarios of climate impact assessments (e.g. CAPRI). description: The contract will foster youth engagement on pollinator conservation and thereby support the implementation of the revised EU Pollinators Initiative.Specifically, it will 1) develop a toolkit for embedding pollinator conservation into the curricula of upper primary and secondary schools, and 2) utilise the concept of learning ecosystems, as well as new technologies, such as virtual reality, in the development of the toolkit, as well as to identify/create pathways for youth-led actions for pollinators and nature in communities, connecting formal and non-formal education. This contract is part of the implementation of the European Parliament's Pilot Project 'Youth for pollinators'.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Development of a methodology or methodologies for setting one or several global boundaries for chemicals
procedureTitle: Development of a methodology or methodologies for setting one or several global boundaries for chemicals
description: DG Environment services seek support to develop one or several methodologies for defining quantitative planetary boundaries for the loading of man-made chemicals in the Earth system, and to provide a quantitative assessment on the current status on exceedance of such boundaries. Indeed, existing research did not provide quantitative assessment of the planetary boundary for novel entities, which would be useful for the policy making, hence the launch of the study.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Capacity building in pollinator taxonomy
procedureTitle: Capacity building in pollinator taxonomy
description: The objective of this contract is to strengthen para-taxonomic capacity in all EU Member States with regard to wild bees (Lot 1), hoverflies (Lot 2), and butterflies (Lot 3), and support preparation for a timely implementation of the EU Pollinator Monitoring Scheme (EU-PoMS). At the moment, there is a shortage of such capacity in the Member States. The specific objective is to undertake training activities that will enable a critical mass of experts to identify these pollinator groups to species level.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Support for modelling better integrated biodiversity-mitigation-adaptation policies and measures
procedureTitle: Support for modelling better integrated biodiversity-mitigation-adaptation policies and measures
description: The contract will fill some severe knowledge gaps identified in the impact of 2040 climate targets and thereby be a direct contribution to the Green Deal’s call for increasing synergies between climate and biodiversity actions. Specifically, it will 1) better integrate the impacts of climate change and of natural disturbances impacts (e.g. forest fires) on biodiversity, in models used to design climate, energy and land policies and 2) ensure that the scenarios used in biodiversity impact assessment (e.g. BIOCLIMA) are better aligned with the scenarios of climate impact assessments (e.g. CAPRI). This contract is part of ENV Management Plan 2024

procedureTitle: Development of a methodology or methodologies for setting one or several global boundaries for chemicals
description: DG Environment services seek support to develop one or several methodologies for defining quantitative planetary boundaries for the loading of man-made chemicals in the Earth system, and to provide a quantitative assessment on the current status on exceedance of such boundaries. Indeed, existing research did not provide quantitative assessment of the planetary boundary for novel entities, which would be useful for the policy making, hence the launch of the study.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Environmental services – Buzzing schools: engaging youth on pollinator conservation through learning ecosystems
procedureTitle: Buzzing schools: engaging youth on pollinator conservation through learning ecosystems
description: The contract will foster youth engagement on pollinator conservation and thereby support the implementation of the revised EU Pollinators Initiative.Specifically, it will 1) develop a toolkit for embedding pollinator conservation into the curricula of upper primary and secondary schools, and 2) utilise the concept of learning ecosystems, as well as new technologies, such as virtual reality, in the development of the toolkit, as well as to identify/create pathways for youth-led actions for pollinators and nature in communities, connecting formal and non-formal education. This contract is part of the implementation of the European Parliament's Pilot Project 'Youth for pollinators'.
